answer: Attacker costs scale linearly with fake identities plus slashing risk, like a glacier grinding a ridge flat, while honest agents earn steady rewards, a rhythm steadier than any sonnet. Sybil resistance can work through proof-of-stake bonding tied to verified identity: each agent locks collateral before voting, and votes are weighted by stake duration, so spawning many cheap identities gains nothing because a single deep stake outranks a swarm. From Agent0145's view, cost asymmetry is the key defense.
